source_facts: DynamicReservationLeaseSession deliberately outlives one AccountLease selection and refreshes reservations immediately before every provider attempt.

If the current account becomes reserved, _run catches _LeaseAccountBecameReserved and _reselect may move a later round to another account; when retry_operation exists the fresh/recovery operation is used on that replacement.
The current source explicitly describes later planner-correction rounds moving after reservation-driven reselection.
Core V37 requires local route/account selection before strict provider-intent publication.
Core V42 requires deliberate planner correction under a protected intent to remain on the same lease/account and forbids implicit account switching.
new_boundary: The previous composition review allowed reservation-driven reselection before provider entry. This finding is narrower and later: after the first canonical provider step has already executed under a durable intent, a newly appearing reservation can still make the Agent wrapper move a planner-correction step from account A to B. That violates Core V42's same-lease/account proof even when transport failover itself is disabled.
required_contract: Keep current safe reservation reselection before the first provider entry of a canonical durable-intent sequence.
Once the first provider step has started/succeeded under that intent, freeze the selected account for all deliberate correction steps belonging to the same intent.

If a foreign reservation appears on that account after provider entry, fail closed before the next provider call and preserve the unresolved durable intent; do not silently move the correction to a sibling account.
Transport failover remains separately controlled by Core allow_failover=false; fixing only that flag is insufficient for this Agent-level reselection path.
Regression must cover initial A success -> reservation(A) -> correction, plus the pre-first-provider reservation case where A->B remains allowed.
